spans.title: A Room Full of Wind
spans.blurb: A visitor steps into a bright, breezy room where curtains stream like flags and two young women in white seem to float above an enormous couch.

spans.title: Looking for the Host
spans.blurb: At a glittering summer party, a guest wanders from bar to library hunting for the host nobody has met, and no one can say who he really is.
spans.spoilerNote: Gives away the charming surprise of how the mysterious host first introduces himself, an early staged moment in the novel.

books.pairNote: Two separate scenes from different evenings; no shared text and neither contains the other's payoff.

spans.title: A Caller in the Study
spans.blurb: A poised young widow receives a foreign stranger who produces a compromising letter signed with her name. Her reaction is not at all what he planned for.

spans.title: Under the Seat
spans.blurb: A young naval officer has an empty first-class carriage, a faint whiff of chloroform, and a suitcase that will not slide under the opposite seat.
spans.brokenNote: The text visibly cuts off mid-sentence at the very end ('the imperative jerking of the'), so the final line reads as a glitch rather than a close.

spans.title: The Wrong Sort of Bees
spans.blurb: A bear with a taste for honey borrows a blue balloon, disguises himself as a small black cloud, and floats up beside a bee tree. The bees grow suspicious.

spans.title: Her Uncle's Wager
spans.blurb: A strange will gives a clever young woman one year to outwit her dead uncle and find what he hid at the manor. She brings the puzzle to a specialist.

spans.title: A Voice in the Darkness
spans.blurb: In the dark of a cold night, a disguised English captain hears a commanding Spanish voice and decides to escort its owner straight into an enemy city.
spans.brokenNote: The passage stops mid-sentence in the middle of a muttered vow ('for my queen—if'), leaving the final line hanging.

spans.title: The Greatest Happiness
spans.blurb: At a stiff family dinner, the quiet cousin everyone ignores suddenly says exactly what she thinks. Nobody knows what to do about it.

spans.title: In Defense of Barney Snaith
spans.blurb: Her relatives trade lurid rumors about a mysterious recluse until the family's quietest woman starts demanding proof, and then stops holding her tongue altogether.

books.pairNote: Both stretches come from the same family dinner but share no text, and each lands its own distinct punchline.

spans.title: The Cult in the Swamp
spans.blurb: New Orleans police follow drumbeats into night-black cypress woods that terrified locals refuse to enter, toward a red glare and a chant no human throat should utter.
spans.spoilerNote: Reveals the cult, its chant, and the carven idol that the full story unveils as step-by-step discoveries, though not its final horror.

spans.title: The Marrow Over the Wall
spans.blurb: A man weeding his garden is nearly struck by a vegetable marrow flung over the wall. The neighbor's apology is stranger than the assault.

spans.title: The Science of Observation
spans.blurb: A sunburned stranger takes the visitor's chair, and his silent host names his war, his regiment, and his trade before he can begin his story.

spans.title: The Count and the Waxwork
spans.blurb: A jewel thief creeps into an empty room to strike down his enemy, only to find a wax figure in the chair and the real man watching.
spans.spoilerNote: Shows the wax decoy and the detective's disguises that this particular case's closing trick is built on.

books.pairNote: The two passages open entirely different cases in the collection and share nothing.
